request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The audit now gets `ROLLUP` and `TOTALS` lines after every change that moves a figure, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- A new `Rollup` service (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollup.java`) works out every person's claimed and due-total, plus the sheet's claimed-total and due-total. Like the screen, the sheet's due-total skips anyone showing `n/a`.
- Each change records the figures before it runs. After its own event, it compares old and new figures and sends out one `RollupChanged` event, only if something moved.
- That event lists the people whose figures changed, in the order they were added. A person who didn't exist before counts as changed, and a name change alone doesn't count. The totals are included only when they differ.
- `SheetAudit` writes the lines in the form the test expects: `ROLLUP sheet= by= person= claimed= due-total=`, then `TOTALS sheet= by= claimed-total= due-total=`.
- Lines are written only after the change is saved, so a refused change writes none.

**Where it's hooked in:** adding and editing a claim; opening, settling and voiding one; adding and editing a person; setting a rate; taking a statement; and changing the sheet's today. Changing today still has no audit line of its own, only the figure lines when figures move.

The cases where nothing should be written work without special handling, because only real differences produce lines: setting a rate to its current value, settling a claim whose frozen figure matches its live one, or re-stating a person whose figures didn't move. The test confirms these.

`Rollup` reads the database directly rather than through the other services. That's because the sheet service now calls `Rollup` itself, so going through those services would make them depend on each other in a loop.
